rationale: Both solutions are correct, well-commented and similarly structured: they track frame state while rolling and run a standard scoring loop at the end. B defines package-level sentinel errors instead of repeating string literals throughout, which is more idiomatic Go and makes the errors comparable by callers. B also uses a single uniform scoring loop, because the tenth frame naturally falls out of the strike/spare/open cases, and a single gameOver predicate guards both Roll and Score. A splits the logic across more helpers (advanceFrame, tenthFrameRolls, validateTenthRoll, tenthFrameComplete), special-cases the tenth frame in Score, and duplicates the error strings. A's tenth-frame validation is somewhat more explicit than B's cumulative 'pinsInFrame < 20' check, which takes a moment to decode. On balance, B's tighter structure and idiomatic error handling make it slightly better.
